bridge_toll_man.text: I remember the ferry from Kyle to Kyleakin. You queued, you waited, and a seagull ate your sandwich. The bridge fixed two of those.
The toll was the worst bit. It was one of the dearest tolls in Europe, for a few hundred yards of bridge. A campaign called 'SKAT' got it scrapped in 2004. I joined, for the singing.

storr_guide.text: The Old Man's about 50 metres high, a rock tower with a thin neck and a bad attitude. A path winds up the hillside, and you can see him from the top of the track. In sun, he looks gorgeous. In fog, he looks like a rumour.
The hills here have names in Gaelic: Sgùrr a' Mhadaidh Ruaidh, Bodach an Stòrr. 'Bodach' means old man. Whoever named him didn't hang about.

pool_swimmer.text: It's 8 degrees. It's not 'refreshing'. It's a medical event with a nice view.
A blue pool, a waterfall, and the Black Cuillin behind it. Honestly the water's so clear you can see every rock. Which makes it worse. You know how far you have to climb out.

wild_camper.text: Scottish access law lets you camp almost anywhere, as long as you leave no trace. No trace means no trace. Pack your rubbish. Don't light a fire. Be nice to the sheep.
I came for a night. That was three weeks ago. The midges are the real landlords. I pay in blood.

then.text: The hall is open and the kettle is on. What more does a man want?
The ballot was last night: the Braes folk, the Portree folk, the lad from the shinty and half of Fiona's cousins, all in one hall with the heating off.
The vote carried, and the Hall is ours. A hundred and forty years since the stones flew, and I still don't quite trust a rule that says yes to us.
The padlock comes off the Braes Hall with a sound like a very old sigh. Somewhere down the road a piper tunes up, badly, and everybody forgives him.
Take a badge. And this heilan has been hanging around the hall since the vote. I think he wants to be on the committee.
You found the old house on the slope. Aye. That's my great-grandfather's, though he never saw it fall.

Now the ballot. The Land Reform Act of 2003 says a community can register an interest and get first refusal when an estate comes up for sale, if the members vote for it. We have the proof, the traders' sums and a team that can win a match.
The Enclosure's liquidator is selling the Braes at auction. Come to the Hall tonight for the count.

The trail has seven stops. The session book in Portree kirk, Seonag in town, the traders' desk in Edinburgh, the auction room, the old court in Inverness, a game of shinty at Fort William and the old house in the bracken above me.
Do them in any order you like but the first few go better in turn. Then come back and I'll tell you the news.

else.text: Welcome to the Braes. The sheep are not impressed by you either.

In 1882 my great-grandfather's township held the hill grazing on Ben Lee against the estate. Fifty Glasgow policemen came up the road and went home again with sore heads. It started something. The Commission came and the Crofters Act followed.
Now the estate is for sale again, and the sellers would like it kept quiet. We can buy it ourselves, the law says, but only with proof and a vote. Will you gather the proof?
Come back when you've seen a bit more of the country. A story like this wants a listener with some miles in their boots.

arc_scot_piper.text: The Hall opened tonight and I'm to play until somebody tells me to stop. Nobody has. It's been three hours. I'm fine. Carry on.
